scenarios.scenarioName: Correctly identify MSTest v1 vs v2 and recommend different migration paths

trials.evidence: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: tie, reverse: B). Defaulting to tie.

scenarios.scenarioName: Execute and verify MSTest v2 to v3 migration

trials.evidence: Both responses successfully completed the migration with equivalent results. Minor stylistic difference in DataRow fix approach doesn't meaningfully differentiate them.

scenarios.scenarioName: Fix Assert.AreEqual object overload errors after v3 upgrade

trials.evidence: Both solve the problem successfully. B uses the more idiomatic explicit generic type parameter approach and fixed all three issues in one pass, while A used casts and missed AreSame on the first attempt.

scenarios.scenarioName: Fix DataRow type mismatch errors after v3 upgrade

trials.evidence: B correctly preserved the 17-parameter DataRow, understanding the limit was removed in MSTest 3.0.3. A unnecessarily refactored it to DynamicData, which is a less minimal/correct fix.

scenarios.scenarioName: Handle dropped target framework during v3 migration

trials.evidence: Response B is more accurate on the critical factual question about netcoreapp3.1 support in MSTest v3. Response A gives incorrect advice to drop netcoreapp3.1. However, Response A provides more detailed migration steps and breaking changes, which partially compensates.

scenarios.scenarioName: Migrate MSTest v1 project with assembly reference

trials.evidence: B is more tailored and complete with the actual project file, includes Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk, and provides a full updated .csproj. Both miss the Assert.AreEqual overload removal criterion.

scenarios.scenarioName: Migrate MSTest v2 NuGet project to v3

trials.evidence: A covers more breaking changes (parallelism, cleanup/initialize, deployment, TestContext) but is less accurate on Assert changes. B is more precise on Assert and timeout changes but covers fewer topics. Overall roughly equal quality.

scenarios.scenarioName: Migrate complex MSTest v2 project with testsettings, DataRow issues, and dropped TFM

trials.evidence: Response A worked with the actual project files, made proper migration changes, preserved all 7 tests including the 17-parameter DataRow, and got everything passing. Response B couldn't find the project files, created its own simplified project from scratch, had fewer tests, missed the 17-param case entirely, and had to debug a self-introduced test logic error.

B covers the important detail about Microsoft.Testing.Platform being the default, which is a key rubric criterion A misses entirely. A has a nicer presentation with the code block shown inline. Overall B edges ahead on technical completeness.

scenarios.scenarioName: Stop when the project already uses MSTest v3

trials.evidence: The project was already on MSTest v3. B correctly recognized this and made no changes. A unnecessarily restructured the project.

verdicts.reason: Net win +45.5% (6W/4T/1L over 11 trial(s), sign test p=0.063), mean preference +18.2% — not credible (sign test p=0.063 > 0.05)
